note: Every statement in internal/ that no test executes. An entry states why the block cannot be executed, never that nobody has got round to it: a missing test is a missing test, and belongs in a test file. Enforced by internal/coverageaudit's own test, which fails both when an unlisted statement becomes uncovered and when a listed one becomes covered. Keys are file, enclosing function, the block's own source text and occurrence: its 1-based ordinal among all blocks with identical text in that function, including covered blocks, in source order (default 1 when omitted). The key survives edits outside the function and edits inside it that do not add, remove or reorder identical statements. TestIdenticalGuardsCannotExchangeCoverage requires separate occurrences so identical guards cannot exchange coverage unnoticed. Every uncovered occurrence is listed separately.

exclusions.statement: return fmt.Errorf("registry: encode the run: %w", err)
exclusions.reason: json.MarshalIndent of the entry the Validate immediately above has just accepted. The encoder refuses exactly two things this entry could hold, and Validate rejects both. A NaN or an infinity in a float64 field: every one of the ten float64 fields in event.ConfigurationPayload (including the nested NotionalAccountConfig and CommissionConfig) is tested for finiteness by ConfigurationPayload.Validate, which Entry.Validate calls. And a time.Time that encoding/json refuses to render as RFC 3339 -- a year outside 0 to 9999, or a timezone offset outside [0,23] hours: Entry.checkSpan refuses a span by calling time.Time.MarshalJSON itself rather than restating its rules, so a span this registry accepts is by construction one the encoder accepts. Restating those rules is how this clause was wrong twice, first omitting the year and then omitting the offset. Nothing else in the entry (strings, a uint32, a uint64) has a failing encoding at all. Both invariants are asserted by tests, so the day either stops holding, this entry is forced to be re-read: TestAnEntryThatValidatesEncodes encodes an entry spanning the whole writable range, TestASpanTheRegistryCannotWriteDownIsRefused pins the span rule, and TestAnInvalidConfigurationIsNeverRecorded the finiteness one. Reachable the moment a field whose encoding can fail is added to the entry without a check beside it.

exclusions.statement: return false
exclusions.reason: Both `!ok` guards parse a string this function already knows is well-formed. The first parses n's own literal: json.Number's only producer in this codebase is a json.Decoder with UseNumber, whose contract is to hand back a string that already matches JSON's number grammar (RFC 8259) — a strict subset of the decimal-or-exponent syntax big.Rat.SetString accepts — so it always succeeds. The second parses strconv.FormatFloat's own output for f, and f is finite whenever n.Float64() returns a nil error on the line immediately above (ParseFloat's only route to a non-finite result is through a non-nil error), so FormatFloat's 'g' output is always a valid, finite decimal-or-exponent literal, which SetString also always accepts. Reachable the moment either producer's own contract stops holding.

Reachable the moment any one of those three stops checking.

exclusions.statement: return nil, fmt.Errorf("strategy: instrument %q: stop fill %q would close campaign %q with an invalid exit: %w", fill.InstrumentID, fill.FillID, campaign.campaignID, err)
exclusions.reason: Validate on a CampaignExitedPayload this function assembled from figures that had already passed sizing's own guards or an accepted payload's Validate. Every field it range-checks is checked upstream, and the RealisedResult re-derivation is formed in the SAME expression order above, so the two agree bit for bit (docs/development.md's fusion rule). The two fields only this payload carries, AverageMoveInN and RealisedResultInUnitN, are quotients of those same figures: reaching a non-finite one needs an enormous numerator or a near-zero denominator, and both were tried against this seam. An exit price large enough to overflow is refused first by the units-stopped decision ('realised result must be finite'), and a DollarsPerPoint small enough to collapse the denominator is refused first by sizing's representability guard ('quantity ... exceeds the largest exactly representable whole quantity'), before any exit is assembled. Until #134 this branch was covered by the below-entry refusal, which was itself the defect: an exit cannot tell a Unit's first stop from a raised one, so it no longer applies the initial-stop shape. If any of this stops holding the guard fires, becomes covered, and the audit reports this entry as stale rather than letting it pass.
